title: Explain KV caching in three sentences.

messages.content: Explain KV caching in three sentences.

KV caching, also known as key-value caching, is a technology that stores frequently accessed data in a cache layer to improve the performance of an application by reducing the number of requests made to a slower backend system. The cache stores data in the form of key-value pairs, where each key corresponds to a unique identifier and the value is the data associated with that key. When the application requests data, the cache is checked first to see if the data is already stored, and if so, it is returned directly to the application without having to fetch it from the backend system.
